```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(mzLibR)
# Every call on this page is answered from a recording of the real bridge, made on mzLib's own
# hand-computed PtmQtl cases, which this package ships in extdata/ptmqtl/, so the page builds
# anywhere. With a bridge installed, the same calls compute the answers.
.mzlibr_example <- mzLibR:::replay_bridge_start()
```

A modification site is rarely all-or-nothing. In one run 15% of a serine is phosphorylated, in the
next 40%. That fraction, the site's **occupancy**, is what changes with age, dose or genotype, and
what two sites can share. Measuring it from label-free data is easy to get wrong: a modified form
that was identified but not quantified is not a zero, a site seen only in its modified form is not
truly 100%, and two sites read off one peptide are correlated by construction. mzLib's
`Quantification.PtmQtl` engine keeps those cases apart.

| question | function | mzLib | method |
|---|---|---|---|
| what fraction of each site carries its modification, run by run? | `ptmqtl_occupancy()` | `SiteOccupancyCalculator.Calculate` (#1369) | intensity occupancy, as MetaMorpheus's `IntensityOccupancy_` |
| the same, for a sample measured as several fractions? | `ptmqtl_occupancy(samples = )` | `SiteOccupancyCalculator.Calculate` with a run-to-sample map | fractions summed before the ratio |
| which two modifications sit on one molecule? | `ptmqtl_pairs(type = "physical")` | `PtmPairEngine.Physical` (#1430) | median co-occupancy |
| which two sites rise and fall together across runs? | `ptmqtl_pairs(type = "covarying")` | `PtmPairEngine.CoVarying` (#1430, #1446) | Spearman's rho, Benjamini-Hochberg |
| does a site's occupancy change with a per-run trait? | `ptmqtl_trait_effects()` | `SiteTraitEffects.Fit` (#1446) | a mixed model per site, a random intercept per replicate |

Every number below comes from mzLib's own hand-computed test cases, so each is one mzLib's tests
assert.

## The input: one row per peptidoform, per run, per protein

Every function reads a tab-separated table with a header row, mzLib's own `PeptidoformObservation`
as columns: `run`; `full_sequence` in MetaMorpheus notation
(`PEPS[Common Biological:Phosphorylation on S]K`); `protein_accession`; `start_residue` and
`end_residue`, the peptide's first and last residue in that protein, counting from 1; `intensity`,
its MS/MS-quantified intensity in that run, **blank** when it was identified but not quantified;
and optionally `previous_residue`, the protein residue before the peptide. Four rules decide
whether the numbers mean anything:

- **One row per (run, peptidoform, protein), never one per PSM.** Two rows for one peptidoform in
  one run would count its intensity twice; mzLib refuses them.
- **MS/MS identifications only.** A match-between-runs transfer is not an identification.
- **Blank, not 0, for "identified but not quantified".** FlashLFQ writes 0 for a peptide it did
  not quantify. Blank those cells.
- **A shared peptide is one row per protein.** Each protein then gets its full intensity.
  MetaMorpheus instead splits a shared peptide across protein groups, so its `IntensityOccupancy_`
  columns can differ.

**mzLib does not build this table for you yet.** It has no reader that turns a MetaMorpheus or
FlashLFQ result into these rows, because that step makes choices: which PSMs count, how a shared
peptide is placed. mzLibR will not make them on mzLib's behalf. You can assemble the table from two
files mzLibR already reads, the PSMs (for runs, proteins and positions) and the FlashLFQ peptide
table (for intensities). One way, with your own choices marked:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Not run: needs your MetaMorpheus search output.
psms <- readers_read_records("AllPSMs.psmtsv")$records
peptides <- readers_read_quantified_peptides("AllQuantifiedPeptides.tsv")$records

# Intensity per (run, full sequence), MS/MS-detected only. FlashLFQ's 0 means "not quantified".
msms <- peptides[peptides$detection_type == "MSMS" & !is.na(peptides$intensity) & peptides$intensity > 0, ]
intensity <- setNames(msms$intensity, paste(msms$sample_label, msms$sequence, sep = "\r"))

# MetaMorpheus writes one value when every protein shares it, else one per protein.
per_protein <- function(cell, count) {
  parts <- strsplit(cell, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (length(parts) == 1L) rep(parts, count) else parts
}

# Your choice of PSMs: targets, q-value below 1%, one unambiguous peptidoform.
kept <- psms[psms$decoy_contam_target == "T" & psms$q_value < 0.01 & psms$ambiguity_level == "1", ]
rows <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(kept)), function(i) {
  p <- kept[i, ]
  accessions <- strsplit(p$protein_accession, "|", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
  spans <- per_protein(p$start_and_end_residues_in_parent_sequence, length(accessions))  # "[69 to 84]"
  before <- per_protein(p$previous_residue, length(accessions))
  ends <- do.call(rbind, strsplit(gsub("[][]", "", spans), " to ", fixed = TRUE))
  data.frame(run = p$file_name_without_extension, full_sequence = p$full_sequence,
             protein_accession = accessions, start_residue = as.integer(ends[, 1]),
             end_residue = as.integer(ends[, 2]), previous_residue = ifelse(nchar(before) == 1, before, ""))
}))
rows <- unique(rows)
rows$intensity <- unname(intensity[paste(rows$run, rows$full_sequence, sep = "\r")])
write.table(rows[, c("run", "full_sequence", "protein_accession", "start_residue", "end_residue",
                     "intensity", "previous_residue")],
            "observations.tsv", sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, na = "")
```

`unique()` keeps one row per (run, peptidoform, protein) however many PSMs the peptidoform has, and
`na = ""` writes a blank intensity for a peptidoform that was identified but not quantified. Check
that the run names of the two files match: FlashLFQ labels a calibrated file `<run>-calib`.

## Occupancy, run by run

The cases file holds several of mzLib's hand-computed cases, each on its own protein, named for
what it tests:

```{r}
ptmqtl_data <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", package = "mzLibR")
occ <- ptmqtl_occupancy(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "cases.tsv"))
occ
r <- occ$records
r[r$protein_accession == "RATIO", c("site_key", "position", "fraction", "unmodified_quantified")]
```

`RATIO` has 30 units of the phosphopeptide, 70 of the same peptide unmodified, and 100 of a
missed-cleavage peptide that also covers the serine: 30 / 200 = 0.15. Every quantified form that
covers the position counts in the denominator, whatever its own sequence.

**Each cell has a state.** Only a `"quantified"` cell has a fraction:

```{r}
r[r$protein_accession == "STATES", c("run", "state", "fraction")]
```

| state | what was seen | read it as |
|---|---|---|
| `quantified` | the modified form was quantified | a measured fraction |
| `floor` | the modified form was identified but not quantified, while forms covering the site were | low, **not zero** |
| `count_only` | the modified form was identified, but nothing covering the site was quantified | present, amount unknown |
| `not_detected` | the site was covered, but no modified form was identified | unknown, **not zero** |

So never average `fraction` with the `NA`s read as 0: they are censored, not absent.

**A 1 can be a ceiling.** When a site is seen only in its modified form, every quantified form
covering it carries the modification, so the fraction is 1. The unmodified form may be there below
detection. `unmodified_quantified` is `FALSE` then:

```{r}
r[r$protein_accession == "CEILING", c("fraction", "unmodified_quantified")]
r[r$protein_accession == "SHARED_POSITION", c("modification", "fraction")]
```

**Two modifications at one position share a denominator**: on `SHARED_POSITION`, 20 units carry
phosphorylation, 30 HexNAc and 50 neither. **Positions count from 1, in the protein**: a protein
N-terminal modification sits at the residue it is on, residue 2 when the initiator methionine was
removed. `readers_read_occupancy()` reads MetaMorpheus's occupancy file, which puts the N-terminus
at position 0, so do not join the two tables on position.

**What mzLib leaves out.** The cases file also holds rows that make no site: oxidation and
carbamidomethylation (mzLib always skips the `Common Variable` and `Common Fixed` categories), a
peptide N-terminal modification, and N-acetylation on a peptide starting at residue 2 after a K.
C-terminal modifications are never sites, because the table does not carry the protein's length.
To keep only some modifications, pass `modifications` (exact names) or `categories` (for example
`"Common Biological"`).

## A sample measured as several fractions

Fractions of one sample are summed before the ratio, as FlashLFQ sums them. Give the run-to-sample
map as a file:

```{r}
fractions <- ptmqtl_occupancy(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "fractions.tsv"),
                              samples = file.path(ptmqtl_data, "fractions_samples.tsv"))
c(runs = fractions$run_count, samples = fractions$sample_count)
fractions$records[, c("protein_accession", "run", "state", "fraction")]
```

`SUMMED` reads 0.3 in fraction 1 and 0.1 in fraction 2. Sample A is (30 + 10) / (100 + 100) = 0.2,
not the mean of 0.3 and 0.1. On `FLOOR_ACROSS` the phosphopeptide was identified, unquantified, in
one fraction, and the site was covered in the other: a floor for the sample. **Map only fractions
together.** Technical replicates are separate measurements of one sample; give each its own name,
and let `ptmqtl_trait_effects()` treat them as replicates of one biological sample.

## Pairs of modifications

A peptidoform carrying two modifications is direct evidence that both sit on one molecule:

```{r}
physical <- ptmqtl_pairs(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "cases.tsv"), type = "physical")
physical$records[, c("site_a", "site_b", "statistic", "n", "statistic_n", "p_value")]
```

`n` is the runs where the doubly modified form was identified (2). `statistic` is the median
**co-occupancy** over the runs where it was quantified (1): 25 of the 100 units covering both
positions carried both marks. There is no test for physical pairs, so `p_value` and `q` are `NA`.

Two sites that rise and fall together across runs are co-varying. mzLib correlates their
occupancies with Spearman's rho, on the runs where both were quantified, and adjusts the p-values
with Benjamini-Hochberg within each family. `type` is required: mzLib has no default between its
two methods.

```{r}
batch <- file.path(ptmqtl_data, "batch.tsv")
plain <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying")
str(plain[c("covarying_run_count", "min_quantified_fraction", "exclude_ceiling")])
pair_of <- function(result) {
  r <- result$records
  r[startsWith(r$site_a, "PAIR_S") & startsWith(r$site_b, "PAIR_T"), c("statistic", "p_value", "q", "fdr_family", "n")]
}
pair_of(plain)
```

`0.7` and `TRUE` are mzLib's defaults, reported because you did not set them: a site enters pairs
only if it is quantified in at least 70% of the runs, and ceilings are left out.

**The trap: a batch correlates everything.** These twelve runs come in two batches, and every site
reads 0.2 higher in the second. That alone gives `PAIR_S` and `PAIR_T` a high rho, though within a
batch they are nearly unrelated. `remove_run_level = TRUE` correlates the two sites given each
run's **level**, the median occupancy of the other sites in that run:

```{r}
given <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying", remove_run_level = TRUE)
pair_of(given)
c(given$run_level_group, given$min_runs_for_run_level, given$min_sites_for_run_level)
```

Given the batch, the pair is unrelated. A pair is tested this way only when it shares at least
`min_runs_for_run_level` runs that have a level, and a run has one only with at least
`min_sites_for_run_level` other sites there. **Remove the run level for a batch or loading shift
only**: if the level follows your design - one condition reads higher everywhere - removing it
removes the effect you are studying. Sites of different chemistry can have different batch shifts:
`run_level_group = "category"` or `"modification"` gives each group its own level, and a
two-column file (`modification`, `group`) as `run_level_groups` gives any other grouping.

- **`overlapping` pairs have no `q`.** When one peptide covers both sites, their occupancies share
  intensities and are correlated by construction, so mzLib reports them but leaves them out of the
  adjustment.
- **`fdr_family`** is the type (`P` physical, `A` co-varying) and whether the two sites are on one
  protein (`intra`) or two (`inter`). `q` is adjusted within it. It is not a target-decoy q-value.
- **`keep_ceiling = TRUE`** keeps runs where a site was seen only modified. Two unrelated sites
  that both read 1 in low-load runs then correlate through detection alone; that is why mzLib leaves
  them out by default.

## Does occupancy change with a trait?

`ptmqtl_trait_effects()` fits, for each site, logit(occupancy) against a per-run trait, with a
random intercept for each biological replicate, so repeated injections of one animal or donor are
not counted as independent evidence. The example is mzLib's `TraitDesign`: six replicates at three
doses, two injections each, built so that logit(occupancy) = -2 + 0.5 x dose + a replicate offset.
First compute occupancy, and write it to a file:

```{r}
written <- ptmqtl_occupancy(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait.tsv"),
                            out = file.path(tempdir(), "trait_occupancy.tsv"))
c(cells_written = written$written$row_count, rows_returned = nrow(written$records))
written$state_counts
head(read.delim(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait_runs.tsv")), 3)
```

The runs table gives each run its replicate, then the trait, then any covariates, each column named
by its header. Then fit (here on the file the call above writes, as this package ships it):

```{r}
effects <- ptmqtl_trait_effects(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait_occupancy.tsv"),
                                file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait_runs.tsv"))
effects
effects$records[, c("protein_accession", "status", "effect", "standard_error", "df", "q", "runs", "replicates")]
```

`TRAIT_SITE` recovers the 0.5 it was built with. **`effect` is in logit units per unit of the
trait**, so `exp(0.5)` = 1.65: each dose unit multiplies the odds of the modified form by about
1.65. The degrees of freedom are between replicates (six replicates, less the intercept and the
dose), because the dose never varies within a replicate. `CENSORED_SITE` is the same site with one
replicate's two runs replaced by a floor and a ceiling. Both leave the fit - only quantified,
non-ceiling cells are responses - so it rests on five replicates and three degrees of freedom.

**Support.** A site needs `min_runs` runs and `min_replicates` replicates with a response, mzLib's
defaults reported in the result. Ask for six replicates, and `CENSORED_SITE` is below support:

```{r}
strict <- ptmqtl_trait_effects(file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait_occupancy.tsv"),
                               file.path(ptmqtl_data, "trait_runs.tsv"), min_replicates = 6)
strict$records[, c("protein_accession", "status", "effect", "replicates")]
```

This answers "does the modified share change?", not "is the modification detected more often?":
floors, count-only and undetected cells are left out, never entered as 0. `q` adjusts over this
call's fitted sites only - not across datasets, and not a target-decoy q-value.

## What these functions will not do

- **No reader builds the input.** mzLib has none yet, so the table above is yours to assemble.
- **No test for physical pairs.** mzLib reports their co-occupancy and counts only.
- **No detection model.** For "is the modification detected more often?", fit a logistic model per
  site with `stats_fit_logistic()` on a 0/1 table of your own.
- **mzLibR does no arithmetic.** Every number on this page came from mzLib.

- [doi:10.2307/2529876](https://doi.org/10.2307/2529876): the random-intercept linear mixed model fitted per site (Laird and Ware, Biometrics 38:963, 1982).
